markscheme: M1: divides £84 by $3 + 4 = 7$ to find one share
A1: £36 and £48 in the correct order
questions.modelAnswer: There are $3 + 4 = 7$ equal parts, so one part is £$84 \div 7 = 12$. The two shares are $3 \times 12 = 36$ pounds and $4 \times 12 = 48$ pounds. Answer: £36 and £48. Check: $36 + 48 = 84$.

markscheme: B1: $7.2$ identified as the number between $1$ and $10$
questions.modelAnswer: Move the decimal point four places to the right to obtain $7.2$. Because the original number is less than $1$, the power of ten is negative: $0.00072 = 7.2 \times 10^{-4}$.

questions.stem: A sequence begins $7, 12, 17, 22, \ldots$ Find an expression for its $n$th term.
markscheme: M1: common difference $5$ used to write $5n$
questions.modelAnswer: The terms increase by $5$ each time, so compare the sequence with the multiples of five: $5, 10, 15, 20, \ldots$ Each term is $2$ more than the corresponding multiple of five. Therefore the $n$th term is $5n + 2$. Check: when $n = 1$, $5(1) + 2 = 7$.

markscheme: M1: expands the bracket correctly to $8x - 12$
M1: collects terms to obtain $6x = 30$
questions.modelAnswer: Expand the bracket: $8x - 12 = 2x + 18$. Subtract $2x$ from both sides and add $12$: $6x = 30$. Divide by $6$: $x = 5$. Check: $4(2 \times 5 - 3) = 28$ and $2 \times 5 + 18 = 28$.

questions.stem: Five numbers have a mean of $8$. Four of the numbers are $5, 7, 9$ and $11$. Work out the fifth number.
markscheme: M1: total of all five numbers $= 5 \times 8 = 40$
M1: total of the four known numbers $= 32$
A1: fifth number $= 8$
questions.modelAnswer: The five numbers must total $5 \times 8 = 40$. The four known numbers total $5 + 7 + 9 + 11 = 32$. Therefore the missing number is $40 - 32 = 8$. Check: the five values sum to $40$, giving mean $40 \div 5 = 8$.

questions.stem: Triangle $T$ has vertices $(1,1)$, $(3,1)$ and $(1,2)$. It is reflected in the line $y = x$. Write down the coordinates of the three vertices of the image.
markscheme: B1: at least two image vertices correct: $(1,1)$, $(1,3)$ or $(2,1)$
B1: all three image vertices correct: $(1,1)$, $(1,3)$ and $(2,1)$
questions.modelAnswer: Reflection in $y = x$ interchanges the $x$- and $y$-coordinates. Thus $(1,1)$ stays at $(1,1)$, $(3,1)$ maps to $(1,3)$, and $(1,2)$ maps to $(2,1)$. The image has vertices $(1,1)$, $(1,3)$ and $(2,1)$.

questions.stem: A metal block has mass $240$ g and volume $80\text{ cm}^3$. (a) Work out its density. (b) A second block of the same metal has volume $120\text{ cm}^3$. Work out its mass.
markscheme: M1: density $=$ mass $\div$ volume, $240 \div 80$
A1: (a) $3\text{ g/cm}^3$
A1: (b) mass $= 3 \times 120 = 360$ g
questions.modelAnswer: (a) Density $= \dfrac{240}{80} = 3\text{ g/cm}^3$. (b) The same metal has the same density, so mass $=$ density $\times$ volume $= 3 \times 120 = 360$ g. Answers: $3\text{ g/cm}^3$ and $360$ g.

questions.stem: A cylindrical tin with a lid has radius $4$ cm and height $12$ cm. Calculate the total area of metal needed to make it, leaving your answer in terms of $\pi$.
markscheme: M1: curved surface area $= 2\pi rh = 96\pi$
M1: area of the lid and base $= 2\pi r^2 = 32\pi$
A1: total metal area $= 128\pi\text{ cm}^2$
questions.modelAnswer: The curved side has area $2\pi rh = 2\pi \times 4 \times 12 = 96\pi$. The lid and base together have area $2\pi r^2 = 2\pi \times 4^2 = 32\pi$. Add the parts: $96\pi + 32\pi = 128\pi$. The tin needs $128\pi\text{ cm}^2$ of metal.
